subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Algorithmic Risk
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Algorithmic Risk.

hook.text: An algorithm makes a million decisions per second. One bug means a million wrong decisions before anyone notices.

buildup.text: Algorithmic risk arises when automated systems make errors at scale faster than humans can intervene.

discovery.text: The 2012 Knight Capital disaster showed that one algorithmic error can generate $440 million in losses in minutes.

twist.text: Testing algorithms in sandbox environments can't replicate real market conditions. Production is the true test.

climax.text: Algorithms amplify both efficiency and risk. Speed is great until the algorithm is wrong at speed.

punchline.text: A million decisions per second. Wrong once. Wrong a million times.

quiz.question: Why is algorithmic risk especially dangerous?
options: Errors happen at scale faster than humans can intervene
